record.original_question: Find a general property of a lifting family in the interval version of Thurston’s algorithm that guarantees convergence for arbitrary kneading sequences, not only preperiodic or periodic ones.

evidence.quote: Question 4. Give a general property for the lifting family which will guarantee convergence of Thurston’s algorithm for arbitrary kneading sequences.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the interval version of Thurston's algorithm for unimodal (or, more generally, piecewise monotone) self-maps of a compact interval. Let f: I → I be a piecewise monotone interval map with a designated set of critical (turning) points, and let K(f) denote its kneading sequence (the symbolic itinerary of the critical orbit relative to the laps of f). Given an admissible kneading sequence κ, Thurston's algorithm produces a sequence of maps {f_n} obtained by iteratively "lifting" along a chosen one-parameter family F = {f_t} of piecewise monotone maps (a "lifting family") so that, in good cases, f_n converges to a piecewise monotone map realizing κ.

It is known that the algorithm converges when κ is periodic or preperiodic (i.e., when the critical orbit is finite), but convergence may fail for general kneading sequences.

Problem. Identify and prove a general structural property of a lifting family F = {f_t} which is sufficient to guarantee that Thurston's algorithm, when applied with F as the lifting family, converges to a piecewise monotone interval map realizing κ for every admissible kneading sequence κ — not merely for periodic or preperiodic ones.
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work (e.g., on Thurston's method for real polynomials and on tower/metric algorithms for interval maps) has established convergence results in various restricted settings — for unimodal maps of high entropy and for periodic/preperiodic kneading data — while counterexamples are known at low entropy. No source found provides a single general property of the lifting family that guarantees convergence for arbitrary kneading sequences, so the question appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: The W. Thurston Algorithm Applied to Real Polynomial Maps
status_evidence.snippet: Convergence of Thurston's algorithm is established in certain real polynomial settings, but not in full generality for arbitrary kneading data.
status_evidence.claim: Convergence results exist in restricted settings; general convergence is not established.

status_evidence.title: Metrics on trees I. The tower algorithm for interval maps (G. Tiozzo)
status_evidence.snippet: The algorithm converges for unimodal maps of high entropy; examples exist where it does not converge for unimodal maps of low entropy.
status_evidence.claim: Convergence is known only under entropy or combinatorial restrictions; failures occur in general.

status_evidence.title: Thurston's method for real polynomials
status_evidence.snippet: Project page describing Thurston's method applied to real polynomials and its convergence behavior.
status_evidence.claim: Active research area; no general lifting-family criterion announced.
